pages: True to her word, circe having lost the game of cards, turns odeyssus's men back into their human forms.
Golden dust flows from her hands, surrounding the swine in a glow and turning them back into their original forms.
Adhering to her promise, Circe puts on a feast for the soldiers and Odeysseus.
Odeysseus could feel the piercing gaze of Ciirce on the back of his neck, thinking she was bitter about the loss...
But all she saw was the ominous shadow in this general's future...
A few days later, the soldiers and Odeysseus are ready to leave Circe's island.
Circe takes him aside and warns Odeysseus of the dangers that lie ahead of his voyage, and the many trials he is yet to face.
Circe percieves the hands of gods playing with the fate of men, and she warns Odeysseus to be wary of the gods' intentions.
Odeysseus is grateful for the warning, and he thanks Circe for her hospitality and for the warning before departing
Odeysseus doesn't let his men know of the warning, making that decision for them as they leave on their ship.
The ship hurt by all the storms it has braved, now carries with her Circe's blessing and the hope of a safe voyage for the men and their captain.
As expected, Posiedon's fury rains upon them with no signs of stopping, This storm was different from the rest, it was more violent and more dangerous than any storm they had faced before.
One could feel the wrath of the ocean god in the air...
They knew this was the one storm they wouldn't survive, and they were right, the ship was torn apart by the waves and the men were thrown into the ocean.
Odeysseus, being the only one to survive, is left to float in the ocean, but surviving from eithe Posiedon's mercy...
Or maybe he has more in store...
All his memories of the voyage, of his family, of himself, comes back to him in a flurry of images as he opens his eyes in Calypso's lap.
For the first time in a long time, he know who he is and what he has to do..
